chunks: 3999 - And he, peace be upon him, said:

A man came to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and said: “I have inherited wealth, and I have come to know that the one from whom I inherited it used to deal in usury. I know that there is usury in it, and I am certain of that, and its halal portion does not sit well with me because of my knowledge concerning it. I asked the fuqahāʾ of the people of al-ʿIrāq and the people of al-Ḥijāz, and they said: It is not halal for you to consume it because of what is in it.”

So Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “If you know that there is a known amount of usury in it and you know its owners, then take your principal wealth and return what is besides that. But if it is mixed, then consume it pleasantly and wholesomely, for the wealth is your wealth. And avoid what its owner used to do.”

For the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم set aside what had passed of usury and prohibited what remained. So whoever was ignorant of it, his ignorance allowed him latitude until he came to know it. Then when he comes to know its prohibition, it becomes forbidden for him, and punishment becomes obligatory upon him regarding it if he engages in it, just as it is obligatory upon one who consumes usury.”

key_terms.الْعُقُوبَةُ: Punishment; legal consequence for knowingly engaging in the prohibited act.
key_terms.تَحْرِيمَهُ: Its prohibition; recognition that the act is legally forbidden.
key_terms.رَأْسَ مَالِكَ: Your principal wealth; the original lawful capital amount.
key_terms.رِبًا: Usury; unlawfully increased wealth through prohibited gain.
key_terms.مُخْتَلِطًا: Mixed; wealth blended such that the unlawful portion is not distinguished.
key_terms.وَرِثْتُ: I inherited; refers to receiving wealth through inheritance.
key_terms.وَضَعَ: Set aside; here meaning what had previously occurred was waived.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inherited wealth if the deceased had dealt in usury?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning inherited wealth connected to usury. If a known usurious portion and its owners can be identified, it must be returned; if it is mixed and indistinguishable, the heir may consume the inheritance while refraining from usurious conduct going forward. It also states that ignorance excuses a person until the ruling becomes known, after which liability attaches.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "A man came to Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) and said: "I have inherited wealth, and I know that the one from whom I inherited it used to engage in usury. I am certain that there is usury in it, and this knowledge makes even the lawful portion unpleasant for me. I have asked the jurists of Iraq and Hijaz, and they said it is not permissible for me to consume it because of what it contains."

Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said to him:
"If you know that there is a specific portion of it that is usury and you know its rightful owners, then take your principal amount and return what is beyond that. But if it is mixed, then consume it with ease and satisfaction, for the wealth is yours. Avoid what its previous owner used to do.

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt) (may Allah (swt) bless him and his family) forgave what has passed of usury and prohibited what remains.
So whoever was ignorant of it, his ignorance is excused until he becomes aware of it. Once he knows it is prohibited, it becomes forbidden for him, and punishment becomes obligatory upon him if he engages in it, just as it is obligatory upon one who consumes usury."
